title: 24th Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 9:01 with committee changes announced and the first reading of a government bill amending the Tobacco Control Act. Most of this part was the preliminary debate on a resolution by MDP's Meekail Ahmed Nasym, which says the Chair's handling of the Majlis hinders its work and asks MPs for their views; MDP members backed it and PNC members opposed it, and no vote appears in this part. After a break, debate began on the housing bill, which is cut off mid-speech at the end of this part. This part continues the debate on the government's Housing (Bohiyaavahikan) Bill, sponsored by Asma Rasheed. Government-side members backed it as a way to make sure social housing reaches people in real need, while MDP members said a law cannot help if no new flats are being built. After a break from 12:03 to 13:02, the Majlis took two committee reports. The Rules Committee report extending the deadline for the General Regulations Act schedules to April 2026, and the Finance Committee report on unpaid HDC rent, were each passed 71-0. The next sitting was set for Wednesday 30 April 2025 at 9:00.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Supported the resolution, saying very few ministers have attended in four months and ministers have not given budget implementation details.
Clarified his remarks on a ministerial residence and an earlier urgent motion on money printing.
Said the bill gives the ministry wide powers, including halting a housing project at any stage, which he saw as a possible obstacle.
Argued that scoring living conditions for points is impractical and suggested a lottery among eligible applicants.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Introduced the resolution, saying the Chair's conduct hinders the Majlis and asking MPs for their views.
In reply, cited missed sittings, ministers not attending, and late-arriving bills as reasons for the resolution.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Opposed the resolution, saying repeated resolutions obstruct the Majlis and he saw no breach of the rules.
On the housing bill: welcomed it and said Feydhoo residents still lack housing on reclaimed land.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said the Chair is acting properly but urged ministers to answer MPs promptly, noting his January question was answered only in April.
Said he belongs to the Maldives Development Alliance, not the MDP, and praised the thoroughness of the report.
Said the money owed could reach billions and urged the finance minister and HDC board to pursue it more firmly.
Said some debtors reopen under new company names, and suggested blocking state services to them until they pay.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Opposed the resolution, saying the Majlis treats the minority respectfully and has passed more bills than the 19th Majlis.
Praised the Finance Committee for a thorough report on HDC's unpaid rent.
Said the Majlis must hold the government, ministries and company heads accountable, and questioned what the previous Majlis and government did on HDC debts.
Said the current Majlis has passed more bills than the 19th Majlis.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Supported the resolution, saying it covers irregular sittings, the Chair's conduct and the minority's limited chances, not only ministers.
Said the report shows large sums owed to HDC and that the money belongs to the public.
Said debtors should pay regardless of which party they are linked to.
Said he doubted the money would be recovered but called on the government to act on the report.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Backed the housing bill as the first of its kind and said a law is needed so social flats go to people who truly need them.
Said flats given out in the past ended up rented out or lived in by people who should not have them, and the law should stop that.
Later presented the Finance Committee report on HDC's unpaid rent and set out its findings and recommendations.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Supported the bill but said flats in Male alone will not fix housing, and urban planning and services in other areas also matter.
Asked for independent oversight, accurate information from applicants and safeguards against corruption in allocation.
On the HDC report, said rent-setting and collection need firmer systems so small and mid-sized businesses can pay while big debtors are pursued.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: As Rules Committee chair, presented the report asking the Majlis to extend the deadline for the General Regulations Act regulations to April 2026.
Said the Majlis expects to finish the remaining regulations during the 20th Majlis, with the Insurance Bill and other regulations in committee.
Said several earlier regulations have already lapsed as new laws on food safety and planning were passed.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Argued MPs must hold government to account and that minority members' chances to question ministers are being narrowed.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Opposed the resolution, saying it mainly concerns ministerial questions and that the opposition gets committee seats and room to debate.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Opposed the resolution, calling it misleading, and compared how similar motions were treated in the 19th Majlis.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Fully supported the resolution, saying MPs' chances to question ministers beyond their portfolios were being cut off.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Opposed the resolution, saying it does not show the Chair acted wrongly, and called on members to act responsibly.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Supported the resolution, citing sittings not held when due and a minister who has not answered a November question.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Opposed the resolution, noting its sponsor was absent, and criticised the MDP's stance on voting for the budget.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Opposed the resolution, saying MDP files many resolutions and urgent motions, and criticised MDP's past record in government.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Opposed the resolution, saying ministers were summoned only 16 times in the 19th Majlis's 1,800 days.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: On the housing bill: called it important and cited a Hulhumale' resident struggling to find housing despite the constitutional right.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Questioned whether the promised 85,000 flats can be delivered, saying no foundation stone had been laid for them after two years.
Said large sums are being spent but projects stall and results are not visible to the public.
Said a bill on paper is not enough if the promises it relies on are not matched by building.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Supported the bill, noting it requires a housing needs survey within six months and a registered list of applicants.
Said an independent commission had found problems with the earlier allocation list, and the bill's rules protect the list from later changes.
Said the bill sets up a housing fund and requires regulations within nine months.

speakers.name: Munthazim Ibrahim
positions: Supported the bill and said some tenants of existing social housing units are not paying rent.
Said a housing fund built from rent could finance more units, and gave an example calculation.
Said families should be able to move from a two-room to a three-room flat as their needs change.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Supported the bill and noted housing is a constitutional right that the government's manifesto promised to ensure.
Said over 3,000 people in Kulhudhuffushi need housing and units promised there had seen little progress.
Said such a law matters for clearing crowded areas of Male.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abdul Rahman
positions: Said housing is a national issue, not only a Male one, with families sharing single rooms on many islands.
Said reducing the pressure to move to Male needs infrastructure and services in larger islands.
Said Hinnavaru has many young people without a home of their own and he expects the bill to help once implemented.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said the deadline for these regulations keeps being extended and the government and Attorney General's Office have made little progress.
Said government members need to raise this themselves for it to move.
Disputed claims that MDP members are absent, citing quorum counts and the allocation of committee seats.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Thanked the committee and said the unpaid amounts are worrying and should reach the government quickly.
Called for a fixed standard when setting rents, saying small and mid-sized businesses cannot bear very high rents.
Said money owed by large companies should be collected, as it belongs to the public.

decisions: Ahmed Zahir (Maduvvari) was named to the Judiciary committee in place of Ali Fazad (Central Fuvahmulah).
The government's Tobacco Control Act amendment bill was read for the first time.
Debate on the resolution on the Chair's handling of Majlis business went ahead with set time shares per party (4 hours total); no vote in this part.
The sitting broke for 30 minutes (10:30 to 11:03) and resumed with the housing bill debate.
The Speaker paused the housing bill debate at midday and the sitting was suspended from 12:03 to 13:02.
The Rules Committee report extending the deadline for the General Regulations Act (Law 6/2008) Schedules 1 and 2 regulations to April 2026 was passed.
The Finance Committee report on unpaid rent owed to HDC was passed; it tells HDC to draw up a plan to recover the money and report back within 30 days.
The next sitting was set for Wednesday 30 April 2025 at 9:00.

votes.what: Rules Committee report extending the deadline for regulations under Schedules 1 and 2 of the General Regulations Act to April 2026
Finance Committee report on rent owed to Housing Development Corporation for leased land and buildings
